title: pvH5PartReader
body:
## pvH5PartReader

Reads H5Part particle files (.h5part, an HDF5 layout used by accelerator and plasma codes) into polydata points with the selected particle arrays; every step stored in the file becomes a time step (time values from the file, or the step index when they are missing). Coordinates come from three scalar arrays chosen by Xarray, Yarray and Zarray (by default the first of x, coords_0, coords0 and so on that exists).

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- If the coordinate arrays are not called x/y/z or coords_0/1/2, set Xarray, Yarray and Zarray, or every particle is placed incorrectly.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this reader, so inspect the output blocks, arrays and time steps on your own files before relying on it.

Native constructor: `H5PartReader`. Identity: `sources/H5PartReader`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

### Inputs

No connected inputs (source/resource).


### Options

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `FileName` | Path of the H5Part file; all time steps are stored inside it, so one file gives the whole time series. Relative paths are resolved from the working directory of the Schemaxis process (in Studio, the directory it was launched from), not from the JSON file's folder; the value is passed when the node is created and must be a constant. Fixed at construction; cannot vary per visit. | `{"minLength":1,"type":"string"}` | `required` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `GenerateVertexCells` | When true, one vertex cell is created per particle; false produces points and point arrays only. Many ParaView filters and representations operate on cells, so keep it on unless only coordinates are needed and memory is tight. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `MaskOutOfTimeRangeOutput` | When true, a request for a time before the first or after the last stored step returns an empty dataset; when false the reader clamps to the first or last step. Turn it on when combining with data that span a longer time so particles do not appear frozen. | `{"type":"boolean"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `false` |
| `PointArrays` | This property lists which point-centered arrays to read. | `{"items":{"type":"string"},"type":"array"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `["REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"]` |
| `Xarray` | This property lists which point array to use for coordinates. | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `Yarray` | This property lists which point array to use for coordinates. | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |
| `Zarray` | This property lists which point array to use for coordinates. | `{"type":"string"}` | `native initialisation / omitted` | `"REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"` |

Execution contract:

```json
{
  "mode": "serial",
  "performance": "unknown"
}
```

Coverage and unbound native properties:

```json
{
  "defaults": "native defaults for omitted options",
  "gaps": {},
  "origin": "generated",
  "output": "native inspection required; explicit output-port selection available",
  "outputPorts": null,
  "qualification": "not-run"
}
```

### Syntax example

Place in `nodes`. Data outputs may be selected by a scene; resource outputs must be connected to a compatible consumer.

```json
{
  "id": "result",
  "filter": "pvH5PartReader",
  "options": {
    "FileName": "REPLACE_WITH_VALUE"
  }
}
```
